{"id": "29a2f0c4-369a-4fd5-8e47-b24d0893f09c", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's what's going on with those two numbers — short answer: it's a methodology restatement, not a footprint regression, and no, you can't pull the old figure back through AWS's live tools.

**Why the number changed**
AWS's Customer Carbon Footprint Tool (CCFT) only ever reflects the *current* calculation methodology for every month it reports — past and present. When AWS updates the model (new `ModelVersion`), it recalculates and overwrites the historical months too. There's no stored "v1 value" sitting next to a "v2 value" for the same month; AWS's own documentation is explicit about this: *"The AWS Sustainability service reflects the most recent model version for every month. You will not see two entries for the same month with different ModelVersion values."*

Since your original 412.7 MTCO2e, AWS has rolled out several substantive methodology changes that would mechanically push totals up, independent of any change in your actual usage:
- A broader v2.0 methodology (applied to Jan 2025 onward)
- Location-based emissions reporting added (June 2025) — which is the specific accounting basis you're comparing here
- Scope 3 emissions (plus Scope 1 natural gas/refrigerants) added to the tool (Oct 2025)

Any one of these — especially Scope 3 inclusion — would increase a reported total just by counting more emission sources, with zero change in your workloads.

**Did your footprint regress?**
No. Since you made no infrastructure or optimization changes, the jump from 412.7 → 468.3 MTCO2e is explained by AWS counting and modeling emissions differently (new scopes, refined factors, model version v3.0.1), not by your AWS usage becoming more carbon-intensive. Think of it as a restatement of the same underlying activity under a new ruler, not a regression.

**Can we get the old-model figure back?**
Not through the console or `GetEstimatedCarbonEmissions` — both only ever surface the latest model version, and AWS doesn't retain or expose prior-version values on demand. The only way to recover the 412.7 MTCO2e under the methodology that produced it is if your organization already had a **Data Export** (CSV/Parquet snapshot via Billing and Cost Management Data Exports) taken back when that model version was live — that file would have frozen the old numbers at the time of export. If no such export exists, that old figure is not recoverable from AWS.

For future-proofing, it's worth setting up a recurring Data Export now, so the next time AWS revises its methodology you'll have a frozen snapshot to compare against, rather than relying on the live API which will always restate history to the newest model.

If you'd like, I can help draft language for your sustainability report explaining this restatement, or check whether a Data Export already exists in your account.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
